review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the repository for uses of largeTupleVector and its three bridge lemmas. They appear in this file, ScaleFirstTuple.lean and TailPrimeRegroup.lean, and always as an explicit simp_rw/simp only list. I looked at the definitions of largePrimeTupleNorm and largePrimeTupleProduct. I did not look for existing simp lemmas that might conflict with the proposed attributes, and I could not run Lean. The risk of the proposal is small: largeTupleVector is a local bridge definition, so the proposed rules do not loop. I found no other simp-interface issues in this file.

findings.excerpt:
lemma largeTupleVector_norm {i j : ℕ} (q : (Fin i → Eisenstein) × (Fin j → Eisenstein))
    (a : Fin i ⊕ Fin j) : norm (largeTupleVector q a) = largePrimeTupleNorm q a := by
findings.problem: largeTupleVector is a bridge definition between the pair form (Fin i → E) × (Fin j → E) and the sum-indexed form. Its three normalizing lemmas are the canonical rewrites: they push norm, product and split back to the pair-side notions (largePrimeTupleNorm, largePrimeTupleProduct, f). None carries a simp attribute (not even a local one). Every use therefore spells the rule list out by hand: `simp_rw [largeTupleVector_split] at he` and `simp only [largeTupleVector_norm,largeTupleVector_prod]`. The same boilerplate is copied in ScaleFirstTuple.lean and TailPrimeRegroup.lean, and TailPrimeRegroup extends the list with largeTupleCoordinateWeight_product. The rules are terminating: largeTupleVector disappears from the right-hand sides. They are directional and have no competing rules, so they are safe simp lemmas.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `largeTupleVector_norm` and `largeTupleVector_prod` with `@[simp]`. Mark `largeTupleVector_split` with `@[simp]` as well, or keep it as an explicit simp_rw because it is a higher-order-pattern rewrite under binders. Then the closing steps of the three proofs can use plain `simp` or `simp only [largeTupleVector_norm, largeTupleVector_prod]` through the simp set, and downstream files stop re-listing the bridge lemmas.
findings.benefit: The reader gets one canonical normal form (pair-side largePrimeTupleNorm/largePrimeTupleProduct). The simp-list boilerplate disappears from the three proofs, and future uses of largeTupleVector cannot forget one of the rules.
